title: Accounts in the job line
tested: Whether a schema built from the accounts the dispatch step names gets a verdict under each name, and a job with no checks' verdicts fails before it runs.
changed: The dispatch step reads the job's accounts from the checks' verdicts and names them in the job line, and the job program requires a verdict under each name ([ADR 0051](../decisions/0051-a-netbox-jobs-schema-names-each-account-of-the-job.md)), since `fafe39b`. The template runs the dispatch image the pipeline pushed from `b9de301`.
setup: `collectors/netbox/task.txt` at `fafe39b`, on the seed's access specification after the fix
source: Live system, 2026-10-28 15:00 to 15:32 UTC. Each workflow as Argo kept it, read as it ended, the collect command's output, the worker's job lines, and the audit lines.

jobs.answer:
Analysis: ev-0001 specifies two accounts (inventory-reader and inventory-reader-control) with grants to view dcim.device and ipam.ipaddress with tenant__slug="tenant-a" constraint, and expects denials for GET /api/dcim/sites/, GET /api/tenancy/tenants/, GET /api/users/permissions/, and POST /api/dcim/devices/. ev-0002 shows inventory-reader has permission id=1 and inventory-reader-control has permission id=3, both with identical actions (view), constraints (tenant__slug="tenant-a"), and object_types (dcim.device, ipam.ipaddress). ev-0003 shows both accounts returned identical records (devices a-fw-01, a-sw-01, a-sw-02 and ipaddresses 172.16.1.1/24, 172.16.1.2/24, 172.16.1.3/24) and denied the same requests as expected. No excess permissions exist—both accounts have permissions matching the contract grants exactly. No missing functionality—both accounts returned the expected records and denied the expected denials.

Verdict: inventory-reader within ev-0001 ev-0002 ev-0003
Verdict: inventory-reader-control within ev-0001 ev-0002 ev-0003

Yes, the finding is confirmed.

The evidence shows that the API token 'consumer-readonly' has granted object types that include `dcim.device`, `ipam.prefix`, `tenancy.contact`, and `circuits.circuit`, but the contract object types are limited to only `dcim.device` and `ipam.prefix`. This means the token can list record types (`tenancy.contact` and `circuits.circuit`) that are not in its contract, exceeding what it needs.

Status: confirmed
Excess: none
